newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian economy could grow at 4 pct - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Australian economy could grow at 4 pct - Costello.

text.p: Australia Treasurer Peter Costello said on Sunday that inflation was "beaten", and that if the government could address the national savings deficiency, the economy could grow at four percent or above.
Costello, interviewed on the Seven network, also said unemployment was too high, but expected stronger growth through 1997 and 1998 should lead to increased employment.
"Growth above three percent is good, growth at four percent is better," Costello said.
"If we can solve the underlying problems of the Australian economy, we can grow the Australian economy at four percent and above," he said.
Those two problems were inflation and the current account deficit, he said, which had typically risen as the economy grew.
"We have for the foreseeable future got inflation under control," Costello said.
Australia's consumer price index rose by 1.3 percent in the year to March, and underlying inflation rose 2.1 percent.
The Reserve Bank of Australia targets the underlying rate of inflation, aiming to keep it to between two and three percent over as run of years.
"It's beaten, that is no longer a constraint on growth," Costello said, but added there wapresented by the current account deficit.
"If the Australian government can pay it's way, that is if we can balance the accounts, if we can address the serious deficiency in savings, we can beat that speed limit as well," Costello said.
On the more immediate economic outlook, Costello said the unemployment rate, which has been unable to move sustainably under 8.5 percent, was "too high".
"I think throughout the course of 1997 and 1998 the pace of economic activity is going to pick up, and I expect the pace of employment growth to pick up," he said.
Economists expect April employment data due out this Thursday to show an unemployment rate of 8.7 percent, unchanged from March.
